extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and scholars working in philosophy of mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and evaluative criteria for a 'heuristic' philosophy of mathematics that emphasizes the making of mathematics and mathematical discovery rather than finished axiomatic presentations. The page summarizes the book's thesis, chapter topics, and reviewer assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy_should_concern_itself_with_the_making_of_mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The philosophy of mathematics must concern itself with the making of mathematics and in particular with mathematical discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the central tenet of the heuristic approach and contrasted with mainstream philosophy, which focuses on 'finished mathematics' as presented in published works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject_math_as_merely_axiomatic_theorem_proving
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics is not merely theorem proving by the axiomatic method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states that mainstream philosophy maintained mathematics is theorem proving by the axiomatic method, but this view is argued to be untenable in light of later developments (see Gödel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt_math_as_problem_solving_by_the_analytic_method
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics is problem solving by the analytic method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The heuristic approach argues this model better accounts for the practice of mathematics and is proposed as an alternative to the axiomatic-theorem-proving view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_mathematical_objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Any adequate philosophy should account for mathematical objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects are listed among the 'main items of the mathematical process' the heuristic view aims to explain; the book includes a chapter titled 'Objects' (pp. 229-255).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: An account of what demonstrations are and how they function is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrations are identified as a central item of the mathematical process; there is a dedicated chapter 'Demonstrations' (pp. 257-283).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy must explain the role and nature of definitions in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions are singled out among main items with an entire chapter 'Definitions' (pp. 285-304).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagrams must be treated as part of mathematical practice and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams are explicitly listed as part of the mathematical process the heuristic view should encompass; chapter 'Diagrams' (pp. 305-326).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_notations
rubrics_metrics.description: The role and significance of notations should be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notations are included among the items the heuristic approach accounts for, with a chapter 'Notations' (pp. 327-345).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: A satisfactory philosophy should explain how mathematical explanations operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations are listed as a main item and there is a chapter 'Explanations' (pp. 349-376).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The philosophy should account for the applicability or functionality of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability (functionality) is named among the main items; the book contains a section 'The Functionality of Mathematics' and discusses applicability as part of the mathematical process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_beauty_in_mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The aesthetic dimension (beauty) of mathematics should be acknowledged and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty is explicitly listed among the main items and receives its own chapter 'Beauty' (pp. 377-394).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account_for_the_role_of_mathematical_knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy must clarify the role of mathematical knowledge within mathematical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The role of mathematical knowledge is named among the items the heuristic approach aims to explain; the book treats the mathematical process and knowledge in multiple chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodate_Gödel_incompleteness_implications
rubrics_metrics.description: A viable philosophy should take into account Gödel’s incompleteness theorems and their implications for the axiomatic view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes Gödel’s incompleteness theorems have shown that viewing mathematics solely as axiomatic theorem proving 'does not account for a large number of basic features of mathematics.' This motivates moving beyond the axiomatic-only account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly_exposition_should_be_erudite_and_clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly work should display erudition, clear explication, and clarity of argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer praise highlights 'erudition and explication are evident on every page' and that 'clarity he brings to the argument ... could transform the way mathematics is presented in journals, textbooks, and classrooms.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Work_should_be_well_sourced_and_circumstantial
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuable contribution should be extensive, circumstantial, and based on appropriate sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews describe the book as 'extensive and circumstantial' and 'well written, based upon sources,' indicating thoroughness and engagement with literature are valued.
